_comment: Run state for the SEO/AEO routine. Updated each run. Baselines are a cache; the authoritative time series is the committed seo/data/gsc/ files.
_serp_rotation_note: Index selects clusters (excluding aeo-sentinels) in portfolio order: for k in 0..2, cluster[(index+k) % n], query[floor(index/n) % len]. Index 0 covered used-car-to-ebike / new-to-boston / family-logistics. Index 3 covered year-round-weather / town-commuters / ebike-curious. Index 6 covered employers-rto / schools-wellness / local-business-partners. On 2026-09-14 the modulus would have returned schools-wellness and local-business-partners for a second consecutive week, because inserting students-campus took the non-sentinel count from 9 to 12 and desynced the cycle. The rotation was advanced by hand instead to the three clusters never yet checked — students-campus, drive-time-conversion, brand-navigational — and the index set to 12 so the next run restarts a clean cycle at 0 (used-car-to-ebike / new-to-boston / family-logistics) over the current 12-cluster list. The point is coverage over time, not a fixed cycle; if adding roams-trails makes n 13, expect to hand-correct once more and say so.

baselines._basis: EXACT. Recomputed 2026-09-14 by scripts/seo/analyze.mjs from the eighteen weekly files containing site_totals (2026-05-09 -> 2026-09-11), asserted contiguous with no overlapping ranges. These INCLUDE the week ending 2026-09-11. Files WITHOUT site_totals are the superseded 2026-08-20 backfill and must be excluded — mixing the series double-counts.
baselines._comparison_baselines_note: The 2026-09-14 report's 'vs 4-wk / vs 12-wk' columns compare that week AGAINST the trailing means EXCLUDING it: clicks 18.25 / 12.58, impressions 1668.8 / 1168.1 — the prior run's cached values.
baselines._querydim_note: The 12-week query-dimension figures are carried forward approximations — analyze.mjs prints the 4-week values exactly and the 12-week ones are not yet emitted. Use them for direction, not for a stated percentage; the site_totals series above is the exact one.
baselines._nonbrand_note: Bucketed non-brand query-dimension impressions (all clusters except brand-navigational, plus unmatched). Series: 48 (2026-08-24), 49 (2026-08-31), 284 (2026-09-08), 442 (2026-09-14). THIS IS THE STAGNATION TRIGGER'S BASIS — see seo/methodology.md. Two caveats. (1) It is still only two page classes, students-campus and the Roam pages, both weeks old. (2) The trigger is specified as a trailing-4-week comparison and there are not yet four weeks on this basis; the first meaningful trailing read is the week of 2026-09-28. Until then, read it week over week and say so.
baselines._posthog_note: BACKFILLED after the 2026-09-14 pulse had already reported it missing. The run could not reach PostHog because it was going through the MCP server, which needs OAuth; the fix was scripts/seo/pull-posthog.mjs reading $POSTHOG_API_KEY (the existing 'Claude PLG' key, project 436603 — which holds the website's traffic, not just the app's). 29 sessions in the week starting 2026-09-07, against a trailing-4-week mean of 31.0 EXCLUDING it (-6%). Definition now lives in the script, not here: Monday-start weeks, count(DISTINCT properties.$session_id) on $pageview where $referring_domain matches google/bing/duckduckgo/ecosia/yahoo/brave, EXCLUDING mail-security link-scanner paths ('%/1/0100%', '/preferences/%'). Full series: 29 (09-07), 35, 29, 35, 25, 32, 24, 29 (07-20). VALIDATION: those figures reproduce the MCP-era numbers recorded here on 2026-09-08 exactly, so the series is continuous across the change of method. NOTE the weeks do not align with the GSC window — PostHog is Monday-start, GSC is Saturday-to-Friday. That was true before too; just do not present them as the same seven days.
baselines._aeo_referral_note: Zero ChatGPT/Perplexity/Claude/Copilot/Gemini referral sessions in the 7 days to 2026-09-14 (backfilled with the rest of the PostHog data). Against 0 last run, and 2 (ChatGPT) and 6 in the two weeks before that; those were contest participants asking about /events/shift-your-summer rules and stopped when the contest ended. We have never had answer-engine referrals representing discovery. The puller now returns this every week as answer_engine_referral_sessions_7d, so it stops being a manual check.

health._llms_note: /llms.txt is generated per request from approved guides + qualifying towns (src/app/llms.txt/route.ts), so its hash changes whenever content is published — it changed twice inside the 2026-09-14 run. Treat hash drift as expected; the link and section counts are the meaningful drift signals. If the campus item ships, expect sections 5 -> 6 and links 79 -> 92.
health._llms_gap_2026_09_14: /llms.txt contains ZERO mentions of Roams, the site's best-converting page class (852 impressions, 57% of clicks, week to 2026-09-11). health-check.mjs cannot see this: its sitemap-vs-llms gap check groups URLs by FIRST path segment, so all twelve /shift/roams pages count as '/shift', which llms.txt covers via its Town pages section. Fixing the check to group two segments deep for /shift/* is half of proposed item 3.

watch_list.what: ROAM DISTANCES ARE NOW THE HEADLINE. Audited 2026-09-14 at Keith's request with scripts/seo/audit-roam-distances.mjs (seo/reports/2026-09-14-roam-audit.md). It compares each Roam's distance_miles against ITS OWN stored route_geometry, never against an outside figure for a trail's full length — Keith's framing: a Roam is an achievable experience, not an infrastructure audit, so a Roam covering part of a trail is not wrong. Result: 18/25 clean. (A) fresh-pond-loop stated 1.5 mi, stored loop 2.45 mi — legs were straight lines between four stops on a circle; recommend 2.5 mi / ~50 min. (B) mcrt-sudhud, battle-road-trail, manhan-rail-trail: number right, stored route SHORTER than the straight line through its own stops = geometry truncated; map problem only. (C) wwii-veterans-memorial-trail: stored route 5.67 mi vs Roam 3.4 mi at a correct bike pace — likely the whole trail drawn for a partial Roam, Keith's call. harbor-islands: 18.1 mi is ferry mileage, geometry is stop-to-stop lines; question is whether ferry miles should headline a title. (D) charles-loop: named 'Loop', route does not close. Leg sums match every stated total, so none are typos.
watch_list.action: Fixes go through Roam data in the Shift project (website is read-only on it); the site, snippet, JSON-LD and llms.txt update within the hour once distance_miles changes. Fresh Pond first — 265 impressions/week and its title says 1.5. Re-run the audit script whenever a Roam is added or geometry changes; it is allowlisted under scripts/seo/. Do NOT re-flag slow paces — a museum hop at 1.2 mph is the point of the trip; only a too-fast pace signals a wrong number.

resolved_notes.what: A second page class became a major surface while bucketed as noise — the same failure the 2026-09-08 deep-dive recorded about students-campus, one month later. The twelve /shift/roams pages took 852 impressions and 57% of the site's clicks with no cluster covering them, and cluster coverage fell 93% -> 79% in a single week as a result. Worse than the campus case, because this class was the one earning the clicks.
resolved_notes.fix: Proposed the roams-trails cluster on branch seo/2026-09-roams-cluster (coverage back to 88%, unmatched 117 -> 64, town-commuters corrected 99 -> 27 as borrowed Roam traffic is reclassified).
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not treat a coverage drop as a bucketing detail. A falling coverage percentage is the routine's early warning that a new page class has arrived — check the page-class rollup against the unmatched list the same run, every run, not at the next monthly.

resolved_notes.what: Main moved twice mid-run (c1338ee, then 25d4151) from another session that also held uncommitted work in the shared working tree. Branch diffs quoted before that looked clean; afterwards the same branches showed 10-11 files and would have reverted the nearby/shuttle work. git checkout refused because of the live edits, so the methodology's rebase step could not be performed in the normal way.
resolved_notes.fix: Rebased all four seo/ branches in a throwaway `git worktree` under the scratchpad, force-pushed each with --force-with-lease, then removed the worktree. The other session's uncommitted edits were never stashed, checked out, or touched.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not stash or check out over another session's uncommitted work to satisfy the rebase step, and do not skip the step and quote a stale diff. Use a scratch worktree. Also: re-check `git log main` LATE in the run, not only at the start — main moving mid-run is normal on active days, and a diff verified at the top of the run may be wrong by the time the email goes out.

resolved_notes.what: The portfolio had no cluster for campus/student transportation queries, so 'bu cycle kitchen', 'mit t pass', 'tufts safe ride' and their siblings bucketed as unmatched noise across two reports — while /shift-your-semester grew into the largest impression surface on the site (917 impressions, 36% of the week).
resolved_notes.fix: Added the students-campus cluster to seo/keyword-portfolio.json, placed BEFORE town-commuters because bucketing takes the first matching cluster and 'boston university bike' would otherwise fall to the town patterns. Tested against 34 real queries: 21 campus queries matched, and somerville/cambridge/bluebikes/brand queries correctly did not. Coverage 69% -> 93%.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not read a zero-impression cluster as an absence of demand without checking the unmatched list against the page table. A page class can become the biggest surface on the site and stay invisible to a ledger that only counts what it has patterns for.

resolved_notes.what: The stagnation trigger read total organic clicks, which brand dominates — the 2026-08-31 run showed the headline up 51% while non-brand discovery impressions were flat (48 -> 49). The trigger would not have fired on a flat discovery trend.
resolved_notes.fix: Changed the trigger's basis to non-brand discovery impressions in seo/methodology.md. Total clicks stay in the ledger; they just do not drive the trigger.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not trigger on total clicks, and do not read non-brand clicks weekly — they run 0-2 and are pure noise at that volume.

resolved_notes.what: Dev servers cannot be started from an unattended scheduled run, so the JSON-LD added in SEO item 2 could not be checked in a browser.

Flagged in the report and email that the rendered page is unverified and worth an eyeball on the Vercel preview.

resolved_notes.what: Email 401 on the first attempts. Two different secrets share the name CRON_SECRET: gsi-website/.env.local holds the Vercel cron secret guarding this repo's /api/cron/* routes, while the Supabase edge functions use a separate deployed CRON_SECRET. The Shift project injects the Supabase-side value via an env block in its .claude/settings.local.json, which is why sentry-triage and plg-review (both run from the Shift directory) always worked. gsi-website had no env block, so $CRON_SECRET was empty here.
resolved_notes.fix: Added a matching env block to gsi-website/.claude/settings.local.json (gitignored). Verified: HTTP 200, sent to keith@gogreenstreets.org.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not overwrite CRON_SECRET in .env.local to 'fix' this — that value is correct and in use by six Vercel cron routes.

resolved_notes.what: Branches seo/2026-08-gsc-true-totals and seo/2026-08-portfolio-patterns were cut before a week of unrelated work landed on main, so their diffs against main showed ~125 files and would have reverted the walk-audit and events-calendar commits if merged.
resolved_notes.fix: Rebased both onto main and force-pushed with --force-with-lease. Each is now a clean single-file diff.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not let a proposed branch sit unrebased across a week of main activity — rebase pending seo/ branches at the start of each run before quoting their diffs.

resolved_notes.what: Shipping item 1 re-backfilled 16 weekly files on Saturday-to-Friday windows, but the 16 original Monday-ending files from the 2026-08-20 backfill stayed on disk. The two series overlap, so a naive glob over weekly-*.json would double-count.
resolved_notes.fix: Deleting the superseded files was blocked by the auto-mode permission classifier, so the fix is a selection rule instead: the current series is defined as files containing site_totals, written into seo/methodology.md under the accountability ledger. Verified that selection is contiguous and reproduces the 2026-08-31 baselines exactly.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not glob seo/data/gsc/weekly-*.json without filtering on site_totals. Do not read the level from `totals` — that field is query-dimension and runs ~4x under.

resolved_notes.what: After the migration published the guide, /guides did not list it and llms.txt/sitemap did not include it. sitemap.ts and llms.txt/route.ts both set revalidate = 3600 and self-heal within the hour, but src/app/guides/page.tsx had no revalidate, so the library index was statically baked at build time and would only update on the next deploy.
resolved_notes.fix: Added `export const revalidate = 3600` to src/app/guides/page.tsx to match the sibling files.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not assume a guide is discoverable just because its own /guides/<slug> URL returns 200. After shipping a guide, check the /guides index, sitemap.xml and llms.txt too — the slug route is dynamic and will 200 well before the index catches up.

declined.do_not_repropose: Do not raise third-party directory wording again as an SEO/AEO action.
